name: Brivaracetam

binding.tissue_or_cell: human brain homogenate (cortex) and CHO cells expressing human recombinant SV2A

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Binds SV2A on synaptic vesicles. SV2A is required for normal neurotransmitter release and is hypothesized to act as a positive modulator of vesicle priming / Ca2+-dependent exocytosis; brivaracetam binding appears to dampen excessive release in epileptic conditions through allosteric modulation rather than block. Sodium channel blockade is a secondary, weaker activity (IC50 in the low-micromolar range) but is not believed to drive clinical efficacy at therapeutic plasma concentrations.

neuroimaging.finding: SV2A occupancy in human brain measured with [11C]UCB-J: brivaracetam ~80% occupancy at therapeutic doses (50-200 mg), confirming the SV2A target engagement at clinically used exposures.

routes.subject_demographics: healthy adult males, multiple ascending dose, ages 18-55

drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: AUC of brivaracetam decreased ~45%; dose increase may be needed

drug_interactions_pk.mechanism: bidirectional: carbamazepine induces CYP2C19/CYP3A, lowering brivaracetam exposure; brivaracetam separately inhibits epoxide hydrolase (carbamazepine-epoxide hydrolysis IC50 8.2 uM), raising carbamazepine-epoxide
drug_interactions_pk.clinical_effect: carbamazepine decreases brivaracetam AUC by 29% (hydroxy-brivaracetam +17%); brivaracetam leaves carbamazepine AUC unchanged but raises carbamazepine-epoxide 2.6-fold

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers (PMs, ~2-4% of Europeans, ~13-23% of East Asians) show ~50% higher steady-state brivaracetam plasma concentrations; CYP2C19 ultrarapid metabolizers (UMs) show modestly lower exposure. FDA label notes that dose reduction may be considered in known PMs.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: secondary mechanism; not relevant at therapeutic free plasma concentrations (~2-10 µM)

demographic_differences.sex: no clinically meaningful sex differences in PK
demographic_differences.age: elderly: ~20% higher exposure due to declining renal/hepatic function; pediatric dosing weight-based
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: hepatic impairment: ~50-60% AUC increase; reduce dose. Mild-moderate renal impairment: no adjustment. Severe renal impairment without dialysis: limited data.

data_gaps_remaining: No direct AMPA receptor binding data — confirmed absent rather than missing

name: Coluracetam

functional.readout: [3H]choline uptake in rat hippocampal synaptosomes
functional.cell_system: hippocampal synaptosomes; chronic in-vivo dosing 0.3-3 mg/kg PO

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Proposed mechanism: enhancement of choline uptake via CHT1 in cholinergic terminals, increasing ACh synthesis rate. Original characterization (MKC-231, Murai et al.) showed restoration of HACU and hippocampal ACh in rats with AF64A-induced cholinergic lesions. Direct molecular interaction with CHT1 has not been demonstrated; the HACU enhancement may be indirect (e.g., upregulation of transporter trafficking).

data_gaps_remaining: No direct binding constant for CHT1
Phase 2a major depressive disorder trial by BrainCells failed to meet primary endpoint (BCI-540); detailed PK never published
No human EEG or fMRI signature

name: CX-1739

functional.readout: synaptic potentiation in hippocampal slice; in vivo respiratory rescue from opioid-induced depression
functional.cell_system: rat hippocampus; human respiratory rate studies

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Low-impact AMPAkine (Type II) — preferentially attenuates desensitization with limited effect on deactivation. Cortex/RespireRx claims ~5x potency over CX-717 (no published peer-reviewed Ki). Mechanism class predicts no Gq-coupled ER calcium release and therefore lower seizure liability than high-impact compounds.

concentration_effect.concentration_unit: n/a — not reported as PK/PD curve

data_gaps_remaining: Phase 2 efficacy data in sleep apnea (results never disclosed publicly)

name: CX-1942

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Water-soluble injectable analog from the CX-1739 series (RespireRx), intended for parenteral use in acute opioid-induced respiratory depression. No primary literature with binding constants or functional EC50 has been published; all references are RespireRx corporate communications.

data_gaps_remaining: Everything — structure, Ki, EC50, PK, all unpublished

name: CX-516

functional.readout: deactivation slowing of glutamate-evoked currents in excised patches
functional.cell_system: HEK293; outside-out patch

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: As a high-impact AMPAkine, CX-516 belongs to the subclass shown by Karst et al. (2024) to trigger Gq-coupled, IP3-mediated ER Ca2+ release at suprathreshold concentrations — proposed mechanism for the convulsant liability that has limited high-impact AMPAkines in clinical development.

routes.subject_demographics: Phase 2 schizophrenia adjunct (Goff et al.) and Alzheimer/MCI studies

off_targets.target: Gq / IP3R (via AMPA receptor metabotropic coupling)
off_targets.clinical_consequence: class-shared convulsant signal in animal models at high concentrations; CX-516 itself was tolerated in clinic but development was halted for low potency / short half-life rather than seizures.

data_gaps_remaining: Numerical human PK parameters (Cmax, Vd, CL never published as full PK)
Direct Ki at any AMPA subunit (no binding-site occupant — modulates allosterically)

functional.readout: deactivation slowing of glutamate-evoked currents in outside-out patches
functional.cell_system: HEK293 expressing GluA1-4 with TARPs; outside-out patch

functional.readout: [3H]fluorowillardiine binding modulation, GluA1-4 + TARP combinations
functional.cell_system: HEK293

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Benzamide-type, like CX-516, but mechanistically closer to the desensitization-blocker subclass; preclinical-only.

name: CX-614

functional.readout: block of desensitization in outside-out patches
functional.cell_system: hippocampal slice + HEK293 recombinant GluA

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Triggers AMPAR-coupled, Gq-mediated IP3R-dependent ER Ca2+ release in cortical neurons (Karst et al., 2024, Synapse) — proposed unifying explanation for the convulsant liability of high-impact AMPAkines including CX-614 and cyclothiazide.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: calcium-dependent neuronal toxicity and convulsions at supratherapeutic concentrations; primary reason this and other high-impact AMPAkines did not reach clinic.

data_gaps_remaining: No human PK or clinical exposure

name: CX-691

functional.readout: kainate-evoked Ca2+ flux potentiation; field EPSP
functional.cell_system: rat hippocampal slice; clinical EEG-correlated psychometric battery in humans

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Benzothiadiazine high-impact AMPAkine. Cardiotoxicity signal reported as one rationale for discontinuation (though specific QT data not in public domain).

neuroimaging.finding: Increased fast-frequency (gamma) power and altered ERP amplitudes at memory-encoding intervals after 500 mg oral; observed in healthy elderly volunteers (Wezenberg et al., 2007).

routes.subject_demographics: healthy elderly volunteers (60-80 y), Wezenberg single-dose crossover

off_targets.clinical_consequence: developmental termination attributed to cardiac toxicity findings; specifics not published

data_gaps_remaining: Direct AMPA EC50 in recombinant system

name: CX-717

functional.readout: fEPSP potentiation; respiratory rhythm rescue in opioid-treated rats
functional.cell_system: hippocampal slice; preBötzinger complex respiratory model

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Low-impact AMPAkine; does not trigger Gq/ER Ca2+ release at therapeutic concentrations, consistent with absence of convulsant signal in human Phase 1/2 studies.

neuroimaging.finding: Restored sleep-deprivation-impaired BOLD signal in DARPA-funded Phase 2 sleep deprivation study (Wesensten et al., 2007).

routes.subject_demographics: Phase 2a ADHD (recently published, 2025); also DARPA sleep-deprivation Phase 2

data_gaps_remaining: Published binding/functional EC50 in standardized assay

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Bicyclic 2-oxopyrrolidone. Developed (originally as EN-101) for cognition; repurposed by Innocrin/Newron for neuropathic pain. Mechanism described in patents as 'glutamate release modulation' without direct receptor binding evidence in peer-reviewed sources.

binding.tissue_or_cell: rat brain SV2A; activity carried entirely by (S)-enantiomer

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: See levetiracetam — only the (S)-enantiomer carries SV2A activity. As racemate, half-doses are inactive ballast.

functional.readout: net charge transfer through GluA channels
functional.cell_system: Xenopus oocyte / HEK293 expressing human GluA

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Benzothiadiazine PAM. Both deactivation slowing and desensitization block contribute. (+)-IDRA-21 is the eutomer.

neuroimaging.finding: Improved delayed matching-to-sample performance in young and aged rhesus monkeys over an oral dose range of 0.15-10 mg/kg (Buccafusco et al., 2004); at individualized best doses, accuracy rose 34% over vehicle on long-delay trials in young animals and up to 18% on medium-delay trials in aged animals, with effects persisting to 48 h after a single dose.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Inhibits synaptic and extrasynaptic NMDA receptor-mediated events in cerebellar granule cells — net effect inhibitory at NMDA despite AMPA potentiation.

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Succinimide-acetamide analog of piracetam. Essentially no primary pharmacology literature.

binding.tissue_or_cell: CHO cells expressing human recombinant SV2A; human cortex membranes

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Binds SV2A on synaptic vesicles, modulating Ca2+-dependent neurotransmitter release in an activity-dependent way. Secondary actions reported include partial inhibition of N-type Ca2+ channels and IP3R-mediated Ca2+ release; these are not believed to drive clinical anticonvulsant efficacy. Critically: no AMPA receptor activity, despite the racetam scaffold and the historical lumping with piracetam family.

neuroimaging.finding: [11C]UCB-J PET shows dose-dependent SV2A occupancy of 10-90% across the 250-3000 mg dose range in humans.

routes.subject_demographics: healthy adults; values from FDA Keppra label and Radtke 2001

concentration_effect.effect: therapeutic plasma concentration for seizure control

pharmacogenetics.phenotype_effects: No clinically relevant CYP-pharmacogenetic effects; metabolism is CYP-independent.

tolerance_and_dependence.receptor_downregulation_half_time: no SV2A downregulation reported with chronic dosing
tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: abrupt withdrawal can precipitate rebound seizures; taper recommended. Behavioral side effects (irritability, aggression, depression) can persist for days after discontinuation in susceptible patients.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: partial inhibition at high concentrations; not clinically dominant

demographic_differences.sex: no clinically significant sex difference in PK
demographic_differences.age: elderly: 2-3 h longer t½ secondary to reduced renal CL
demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: Renal: dose-reduce per CrCl; hemodialysis removes ~50% in 4 h. Hepatic: no adjustment needed except severe (Child-Pugh C: 50% dose reduction).

name: LY-404187

functional.readout: fEPSC potentiation (CV-2) in neonatal rat CA1
functional.cell_system: hippocampal slice (CA3-CA1) and HEK293 recombinant

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: High-impact AMPA PAM; binds at the dimer interface of GluA ligand-binding domains. Strong preference for the flip splice variant gives some intrinsic regional/subunit selectivity.

off_targets.target: Gq / IP3R (class-shared high-impact metabotropic AMPA coupling)
off_targets.clinical_consequence: convulsant in vivo at supratherapeutic doses — limited utility despite high potency

data_gaps_remaining: Quantitative EC50 in standardized recombinant assay

functional.readout: fEPSP potentiation; chronic dosing → hippocampal cell proliferation
functional.cell_system: rat hippocampus in vivo and slice

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Biarylpropylsulfonamide AMPA PAM; high-impact subgroup. Note: LY-451646 (the (R,R) diastereomer) and mibampator (LY-451395, also (R)-enantiomer) are closely related — sources sometimes conflate them.

functional.readout: BDNF upregulation in hippocampus; neuroprotection in MPTP and 6-OHDA Parkinson's models
functional.cell_system: in vivo

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Sustained AMPA potentiation → BDNF upregulation → neurotrophic / neurogenic effects in rodents. Class-shared high-impact mechanism with attendant Gq/Ca2+ liability at higher exposures.

functional.readout: PI hydrolysis; functional studies
functional.cell_system: brain slice; transfected cell line

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Functional M1 agonism + acetylcholine release enhancement in rat cortex/hippocampus. Pursued in Japan in the 1990s for dementia.

functional.readout: current potentiation
functional.cell_system: expressed nAChR

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: PKA-dependent nAChR potentiation; Ca2+ channel enhancement; GABA turnover increase in cortex/hippocampus after chronic dosing; ACh release enhancement in frontal cortex (microdialysis). Mechanistically the most pleiotropic of the cognitive-targeting racetams.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Hepatotoxicity in beagle dogs at high chronic doses halted Western development; clean in rodent studies. Japanese program continued and reported acceptable human safety.

functional.readout: spatial reference memory enhancement in rats
functional.cell_system: in vivo behavioral

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Originally Organon, later Schering-Plough then Merck (MK-8777). Phase 2 in MDD (NCT00610649) and ADHD; failed to demonstrate efficacy.

name: Oxiracetam

functional.readout: [3H]choline uptake in rat hippocampal synaptosomes after chronic dosing
functional.cell_system: hippocampal synaptosomes; 100 mg/kg/day x several days

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Hippocampal/cortical cholinergic activation (HACU upregulation, ACh release); modest effects on phospholipid turnover. Like piracetam, the direct molecular target remains poorly defined — the functional effects sit downstream of cholinergic tone.

demographic_differences.renal_or_hepatic: renal impairment dramatically prolongs t½ (8 h → 10-68 h); dose reduction required

data_gaps_remaining: Direct receptor binding constants (essentially none exist because target is ill-defined)

functional.readout: potentiation of glutamate-evoked currents in Xenopus oocytes
functional.cell_system: Xenopus oocytes expressing GluRA-D

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Sulfonamide-class AMPAkine; suppresses desensitization. Flop-selectivity is mechanistically important — flop is enriched in adult forebrain, flip in developing brain and cerebellum.

Hydrazide analog of phenylpiracetam, first reported by a Russian group in 1980 as part of an anticonvulsant series. Crosses BBB well per radiolabeled biodistribution in mice. Mechanism is largely speculative; original characterization framed it as an anticonvulsant rather than a stimulant.

name: Piracetam

functional.readout: potentiation of glutamate-evoked currents (in vitro)
functional.cell_system: hippocampal slice; reported only at mM concentrations

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: After 60+ years, no consensus mechanism. Proposed: (1) membrane fluidity modulation via interaction with polar phospholipid head groups, (2) increased AMPA receptor density in aged brain, (3) facilitation of cholinergic neurotransmission, (4) improved erythrocyte deformability (relevant to cerebrovascular indications). None of these has been quantified to a Ki or EC50 at therapeutic concentrations.

neuroimaging.finding: Modest increases in interhemispheric EEG coherence in elderly subjects; small fMRI BOLD increases in language regions after acute dosing. Effect sizes generally small and inconsistent across studies.

tolerance_and_dependence.withdrawal_syndrome: no characterized somatic withdrawal; rare reports of psychological rebound

demographic_differences.age: modestly prolonged t½ in elderly secondary to declining renal CL

data_gaps_remaining: Direct molecular target at therapeutic concentrations — genuinely unknown after decades

functional.readout: increased synaptosomal HACU after acute and chronic dosing
functional.cell_system: hippocampal synaptosomes

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Cholinergic activation via HACU enhancement; no direct receptor binding. The basic amine side chain is the distinguishing structural feature — likely responsible for higher brain penetration than piracetam/oxiracetam.
Cyclic pyrrolizine-dione racetam analog. Showed mild cognitive effects in early Parke-Davis animal screens but never characterized mechanistically. Discontinued before meaningful clinical work.

functional.readout: (S)-AMPA-evoked neurotransmitter release potentiation; ACh release in hippocampus
functional.cell_system: rat hippocampal and frontal cortex slice

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Benzothiadiazine class — likely high-impact mechanistic profile. Servier development program included anti-aging cognitive enhancement angle.

off_targets.clinical_consequence: Chronic dosing reversed age-related lipid peroxidation increases and Cu/Zn-SOD decreases in aged rat prelimbic cortex — likely downstream of trophic effects rather than direct antioxidant action.

name: Seletracetam

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: SV2A modulator — pyrrolidone with difluorovinyl substituent. Discontinued by UCB in favor of brivaracetam despite higher SV2A affinity; reasons not fully disclosed but likely PK/tolerability.

data_gaps_remaining: Human Phase 2 efficacy/safety data (limited public disclosure)

name: Sunifiram

functional.readout: reversal of NBQX-induced amnesia in mouse passive avoidance; reversal of kynurenate block of NMDA-mediated [3H]NA release
functional.cell_system: in vivo behavior; rat hippocampal slice

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mechanism of action genuinely uncertain. Authors of the original characterization suggest indirect AMPA potentiation, possibly via glycine-site facilitation of NMDA receptors leading to AMPA insertion. No primary receptor target has ever been identified by direct binding assay.

data_gaps_remaining: Direct binding constant at any receptor
Independent replication of antiamnesic activity outside the original Italian group

name: Unifiram

functional.target: excitatory synaptic transmission (rat hippocampus, in vitro)
functional.readout: concentration-dependent fEPSP enhancement
functional.cell_system: hippocampal slice

pharmacology.downstream_signalling: Mechanism uncertain — same caveats as sunifiram. Reported 1000x more potent than piracetam in scopolamine-amnesia reversal, but this potency advantage relies on a single research-group's behavioral series.

data_gaps_remaining: Direct receptor binding at any target
Independent confirmation of preclinical efficacy outside the original group

shared_mechanism: Two genuinely distinct mechanism classes share this folder for historical/structural reasons. (1) AMPAkines are positive allosteric modulators of AMPA-type ionotropic glutamate receptors, splitting into 'high-impact' (Type I — large modulation, Gq-coupled metabotropic AMPA signaling with ER Ca2+ release, convulsant liability; CX-516, CX-614, biarylpropylsulfonamides) and 'low-impact' (Type II — desensitization-focused, minimal Gq coupling, safer; CX-717, CX-1739, Org 26576). (2) Racetams are a structurally-defined family of 2-oxopyrrolidone derivatives with no shared receptor target: piracetam/aniracetam/oxiracetam/pramiracetam are loosely 'cholinergic-via-HACU' with weak or absent direct receptor binding; aniracetam is a genuine but low-potency AMPA PAM; levetiracetam/brivaracetam/seletracetam are SV2A ligands and have no AMPA activity despite the shared scaffold; nefiracetam is pleiotropic (Ca channels, nAChR, GABA); coluracetam is an HACU enhancer at CHT1; phenylpiracetam adds a DAT-inhibitor stimulant component. Sunifiram and unifiram are 'racetam-adjacent' piperazine derivatives whose AMPA mechanism has never been demonstrated directly.
shared_pk_summary: Racetams typical: high oral bioavailability (often ~100%), negligible protein binding, predominant renal elimination of unchanged drug (piracetam, levetiracetam, oxiracetam), short-to-moderate plasma half-life (3-8 h). Brivaracetam and aniracetam diverge: brivaracetam undergoes hepatic amidase hydrolysis + CYP2C19 hydroxylation; aniracetam has ~0.2% systemic bioavailability with extensive first-pass to N-anisoyl-GABA (the putative active metabolite). AMPAkines have generally poor published human PK — most never reached substantial clinical exposure. The recurring failure mode for AMPAkines in trials is dose-limiting CNS adverse events (often before efficacy is reached) plus low CNS penetration for many compounds.
shared_safety: AMPAkines — high-impact subclass carries demonstrated convulsant liability in animal models (Gq-coupled ER Ca2+ mechanism, Karst et al. Synapse 2024); low-impact subclass appears safer but is also less efficacious. The Cortex/Org programs were terminated primarily for low efficacy at tolerated doses (high-impact) or cardiotoxicity signals (CX-691/farampator). Pharma essentially exited the AMPAkine cognitive-enhancement space ~2014. Racetams — generally a benign safety profile: piracetam/oxiracetam/aniracetam are well-tolerated at gram-scale doses; major caveat is the behavioral adverse-event signal with SV2A ligands (irritability, depression, aggression — levetiracetam especially), which is mechanism-specific to SV2A rather than to the racetam scaffold. Phenylpiracetam carries a stimulant component and is WADA-banned in sport.
sar_summary: AMPAkines — three principal chemotypes: (1) benzamides (CX-516, CX-546) — first generation, modest potency, mixed deactivation/desensitization; (2) benzothiadiazines (IDRA-21, CX-691, S-18986) — typically higher potency, often high-impact, increase EEG gamma; (3) biarylpropylsulfonamides (LY-404187, LY-451646, LY-503430, mibampator) — Lilly series, ~1000-fold more potent than CX-516, almost universally high-impact; (4) benzoxazines (CX-614) — rigid bicyclic, very potent desensitization blockers. Flip-vs-flop splice-variant selectivity is a real SAR axis (cyclothiazide → flip; PEPA → flop) but underexploited clinically. Racetams — 2-oxopyrrolidone is the structural defining core; substitution patterns radically change pharmacology: 4-aryl (aniracetam) adds AMPA modulation; 4-propyl/butyl (brivaracetam, levetiracetam) yields SV2A binding with no AMPA activity; 4-phenyl (phenylpiracetam) adds DAT-inhibitor stimulant component; basic amine side chains (pramiracetam) increase brain penetration; bicyclic constraints (dimiracetam, rolziracetam) variably retain or lose activity. The shared 'racetam' label across these structurally similar but mechanistically unrelated compounds is one of the most misleading naming conventions in modern neuropharmacology.
